fatal_errors: The proposed material is a single-phase TiVNbTa-type refractory HEA, whereas the target is as-cast dual-phase AlCoCrFeNi2.1 with FCC and B2 phases.
The hypothesis attributes brittleness to impurity-induced segregation and interstitial depletion, but the cited evidence demonstrates matrix softening rather than toughness loss or brittle fracture.
It misses the governing L12 ordering, elevated antiphase-boundary energy, planar slip, jagged B2/FCC phase-boundary stress concentrations, and associated plastic instability.
It does not predict the non-monotonic ductile-brittle-ductile response, including minimum ductility near 600°C and recovery near 750°C.
The proposed experiment does not localize dislocation pile-ups or crack initiation at jagged phase-boundary tips or exclude grain-boundary impurity segregation.
explanation: The response is broadly aligned with thermal-aging-induced changes in an HEA and offers a controllable aging/impurity experiment, but it reconstructs a different alloy system and mechanism. Its evidence validly supports impurity-assisted alpha-Ti precipitation and softening in TiVNbTa aged at 700°C; it does not support the extrapolation from softening to brittle fracture or toughness loss. The temperature and service boundaries are vague and omit the target 550–750°C embrittlement window and recovery above it. The falsification rule can test the proposed segregation claim, but it is generic and does not discriminate impurity segregation from the target ordering/phase-boundary mechanism. Consequently, this is neither an exact nor a well-supported alternative explanation of the target behavior.
